sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia-European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 2013)
Colombia-Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Taxation Agreement
Colombia-Chile Free Trade Agreement and Tax Agreement
Colombia-Mexico Alianza del Pacífico Free Trade Agreement and Additional Protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006 (FATF international standards), Ley 1762 de 2015 (AML amendments), Ley 2010 de 2019 (UBO reporting framework), Decreto 1068 de 2015 (Sarlaft obligations for supervised entities), Resolución 1507 de 2021 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales), Circular Externa 100-000005 de 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or supervisory authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing country is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, Colombian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian incorporation representative or attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the shareholder or incorporating party signs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization, followed by certified Spanish translation when executed in a non-Spanish language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and notarized identity certifications for ultimate beneficial owners and legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority; certified copies from a notary public of the holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only when the Colombian Cámara de Comercio or Superintendencia requires notarial certification abroad; otherwise certified translation by a Colombian qualified interpreter/translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against Colombian political-exposure sources (Procuraduría, Comptroller, and judicial databases), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU restrictive measures list, and local Boletín de Responsables Fiscales; UBOs, directors, and legal representatives must also be screened against internal anti-money-laundering red flags; negative screening results must be documented and retained in the Sarlaft file for at least 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Confecámaras - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rue.com.co; e-services of the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, www.ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in the Latin alphabet, may be in Spanish, English, or any language transliterated into the Latin alphabet; the name must be singular, not deceptive or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and must include the suffix 'S.A.S.'; accents and punctuation do not distinguish names for homonymy purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) business days of rejection, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration (recurso de reposición) before the same Cámara de Comercio; if denied, within ten (10) business days the applicant may file a subsidiary appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio, attaching the rejection notice, a new name-clearance certificate if applicable, and legal argument; the name reservation can be renewed once if requested before the original 30-day window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a P.O. Box; a virtual office or business service address is permissible for a B2B SaaS entity only where it is a physical municipal address within the registered domicile and legal notices, correspondence, and official inspections can be received. The virtual office must be designated as 'oficina virtual' in the RUES filing and should be supported by a service agreement; however, the Cámara de Comercio and DIAN may require evidence that the company actually directs its operations from that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of an unannounced inspection by the Cámara de Comercio or DIAN is approximately 5% for a newly incorporated unlicensed SaaS company, increasing to approximately 15% if the entity invoices significant VAT, applies for advance tax rulings, or has foreign operations requiring transfer pricing documentation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance (certificado de homonimia) and registration file opening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published in the chamber's annual fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille issuing authority and/or Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of power of attorney and incorporation private document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public (Notaría) of selected corporate domicile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence of UBOs and corporate foreign shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for a low-risk B2B SaaS entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/sanctions screening and UBO background verification (subscription or search fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML/CFT screening data provider (e.g., LexisNexis, World-Check, or local equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual per-entity license / transactional search cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office registered-address setup fee (first month)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed virtual-office service provider in the domicile municipality
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark monthly rental fee for a commercial service address

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile Registry (RUES) registration fee - minimum tariff
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff based on the company's minimum paid-in capital and asset value

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO registration filing with the Superintendencia de Sociedades (RUBF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration fee; cost is covered by the annual supervision contribution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Ley 1258 de 2008) on the Simplified Stock Corporation (S.A.S.), arts. 2, 4, 5, 22 and 45; Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio), arts. 98 et seq.; Law 1429 of 2010 on business formalization simplification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the chosen registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating the single business registry RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social); final tax registration with DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document with integrated Bylaws); public deed (Escritura Pública) is required only if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under art. 4 of Law 1258/2008, the S.A.S. has no statutory minimum capital; the Bylaws freely set capital, cash subscriptions may be paid within up to two years, and no escrow or blocked-account requirement applies. Non-resident capital must be channeled through the foreign-exchange market and registered with Banco de la República as FDI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned incorporators, acting as the founding shareholders of [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S.: (1) RATIFY the execution of the private incorporation document and the adoption of the Bylaws executed under Law 1258 of 2008; (2) ACCEPT the full subscription of the authorized share capital of COP [•], allocated among the undersigned in the proportions set out in the Bylaws; (3) ADOPT [registered address], [city], Republic of Colombia, as the registered office and legal domicile; (4) APPOINT [NAME] as Legal Representative and [NAME] as Deputy Legal Representative, with the powers set forth in the Bylaws; and (5) AUTHORIZE the Legal Representative to complete all registrations, tax filings, and opening of bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-validation and reservation of corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RUES online portal of the Cámara de Comercio of the intended domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a homonymy search in the RUES database to confirm that the proposed corporate name is distinct from existing registered entities; reserve the name electronically for up to 30 days and download the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of each incorporator (cédula de ciudadanía or valid passport)
Proposed corporate name and activity description
Contact email and physical address of the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or misleadingly similar, the RUES system issues an automatic rejection; select an alternative name and resubmit the reservation the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of incorporation document and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notaría) for signature authentication, followed by filing with the chamber of commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución including the complete Bylaws; all founding shareholders sign, and their signatures are authenticated before a notary (or directly before the chamber staff). No public deed is required unless real estate is contributed to the corporate estate.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation document and Bylaws compliant with Law 1258/2008
Notarial authentication certificate if signed before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On notarial refusal, cure the identified defects (e.g., incomplete capital or representation clauses) and re-present the document; resubmission within 5 business days avoids duplicate fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce and issuance of certificate of existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social, integrated with the RUES national registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation package at the chamber's registration window or through its virtual office; pay the registration rights (derechos de inscripción) and the registry tax (impuesto de registro); upon approval, the chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which evidences legal personality.
required_dossiers: Incorporation document with notarial authentication (where applicable)
RUES pre-registration form (Formulario de matrícula mercantil)
Acceptance of office (aceptación del cargo) signed by the legal representative and deputy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry official raises objections, the chamber issues an observation notice; the incorporators must correct and resubmit the document within 10 business days through the RUES module, after which the file is deemed abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (NIT and RUT) and foreign-investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) via the chamber's integrated system; Banco de la República for FDI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The chamber automatically transmits incorporation data to DIAN for assignment of the corporate NIT and pre-registration of the RUT; the legal representative must finalize the RUT (address, activity ISIC 6201, tax categories) on DIAN's electronic portal. If non-resident shareholders contributed capital, register the investment as FDI with Banco de la República and obtain the exchange channeling certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Finalized RUT form on the DIAN portal
Proof of payment or remittance against the capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT application, correct the inconsistent data (activity code, address, responsible status) and resubmit electronically; if FDI registration is queried, supplement the beneficial-ownership declarations and currency-channeling proof before the Banco de la República.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of corporate books and initial governance acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (books registry); shareholders' meeting as supreme corporate body
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open and register the mandatory corporate books (libros de comercio: shareholders' meeting minutes book, share registry, and shareholders' registry) with the chamber; record the authorization of the legal representative, adopt the fiscal year ending December 31, and ratify the appointment acts in the minutes book; obtain the stamp of registration on the first folio of each book.
required_dossiers: Certified initial entries in the corporate books signed by the legal representative
Shareholders' meeting minutes approving the opening of books
Receipt of payment of book-registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books are rejected for formal defects, recertify the entries and resubmit within the term granted by the chamber; late registration subjects the company to the chamber's standard fines for untimely commercial registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Treasury (Secretaría de Hacienda) of the business domicile for the industry-and-commerce registration; Curaduría Urbana for land-use certificates; Ministry of ICT (MinTIC) as the sector authority for software services (non-licensing registration only)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Industria y Comercio (municipal ICA operating tax registration) together with the Certificado de Uso de Suelo (land-use certificate) for the physical office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national-level licensing; municipal environmental authority (e.g., Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente in Bogotá) for local control
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based enterprise software development under ISIC 6201 does not trigger an environmental license; the activity is classified as 'No requiere licencia ambiental' and is outside the mandatory EIA list under Decree 1076 of 2015, Title 6.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluents or VOC emissions; domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewerage limits under Resolution 0631 of 2015; IT and e-waste must be managed through certified collectors under Resolution 1512 of 2010; building HVAC noise must comply with local municipal ordinance limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) issued by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos for the leased office; enrollment of the company and employees with an Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL); compliance with workplace hygiene and safety standards under Resolution 2400 of 1979 and Decree 1072 of 2015 (SG-SST); structural occupancy clearance follows the building's municipal occupancy permit and the lease's land-use certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: Sede Electrónica / MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) at https://www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Colombian SAS, the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) is granted automatically upon incorporation before the Cámara de Comercio. The entity must then complete its registration in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) via DIAN's Sede Electrónica, submitting the certificate of existence and legal representation, identification documents of shareholders and legal representative, the bylaws, and the election of IVA, export, and e-invoicing responsibilities. A non-resident foreign SaaS vendor acting without a Colombian entity must appoint a legal representative or fiscal agent in Colombia, present apostilled incorporation documents and a power of attorney, and file the RUT application with DIAN to obtain a NIT and VAT registration before supplying digital services into Colombia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists; the Colombian SAS is mandatorily taxed as a distinct corporate entity. Relevant available elections: (i) optional adherence to the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for eligible smaller taxpayers, which consolidates income tax and IVA into a single return; (ii) election of IVA filing frequency (bimestral, cuatrimestral, or anual) according to gross income and export volume; (iii) the 'no responsable de IVA' election for taxpayers below the 3,500-UVT turnover threshold, which is not available to a SAS making taxable B2B service supplies; and (iv) classification in the RUT as 'responsable de IVA — exportador de servicios' to access zero-rating and input VAT recovery. Colombia applies OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch restrictions under domestic law and DUR 1625/2016, so cross-border hybrid branch or hybrid instrument structures are recharacterized for Colombian tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) — Colombian Value Added Tax; supplementary impuesto nacional al consumo applies to selected foodstuffs and hospitality; non-resident digital service providers are required to charge the 19% IVA on digital and software services supplied to Colombian residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gross income exceeding 3,500 UVT in the preceding year (COP 164,727,500 for tax year 2024; COP 174,296,500 for tax year 2025) triggers mandatory IVA registration. Nevertheless, any SAS performing taxable supplies of services, including B2B Enterprise SaaS, must register as a VAT-responsible person and adopt electronic invoicing irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time clearance. Each invoice must be issued as a Factura Electrónica de Venta in XML conforming to UBL 2.1 or CII, transmitted to DIAN through an authorized proveedor tecnológico or DIAN's free invoicing application, validated by DIAN through MUISCA before delivery to the customer, and assigned a unique CUNE (Código Único de Numeración de Factura) and a QR code. Export invoices must carry the 'exportación de servicios' modality, state the zero-rated/exempt nature of the service, and identify the foreign buyer's tax domicile and tax ID. High-volume issuers must integrate with DIAN web services via API. Non-compliance invalidates the invoice for fiscal purposes, disallows input VAT credits, prevents the substantiation of zero-rated export claims, and exposes the taxpayer to fines measured in UVT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: B2B SaaS subscriptions, licenses, cloud implementation, and support services qualify for the 0% IVA rate as exports of services under Article 481 of the Estatuto Tributario and DUR 1625/2016 if all of the following conditions are met: (a) the contracting party is a non-resident without domicile, establishment, or permanent establishment in Colombia; (b) the service is used and effectively exploited exclusively outside Colombia; (c) the Colombian SAS is registered in the RUT as an exporter of services under ISIC 6201; and (d) the consideration is collected through authorized Colombian foreign-exchange channels or documented cross-border remittances. Services rendered to a foreign client but consumed inside Colombia, such as services supporting a local Colombian user base or delivered through Colombian infrastructure for local use, remain subject to 19% IVA. DIAN's official doctrine requires objective evidence of offshore use and exploitation, including client access from foreign territories, foreign contract execution, and records demonstrating that the platform's users are located outside Colombia.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs/Service Export Documentation: for services, the executed export contract or order form identifying the foreign beneficiary and the offshore utilization requirement (no Bill of Lading applies to SaaS transactions); if goods are involved, the Declaración de Exportación (DEX) processed via the SIGLO/VUCE platforms
Electronic export invoice: Factura Electrónica de Venta marked as 'Exportación de Servicios', validated by DIAN, and bearing the CUNE and QR code

Inward Remittance Certificate: Declaración de Cambio and foreign-exchange settlement certificate issued by an authorized Colombian intermediary under Banco de la República rules, evidencing the reintegro de divisas
RUT extract (Certificado de Régimen Tributario) demonstrating the 'Exportador de Servicios' classification and the CIIU/ISIC activity code 6201

Substantiation of exclusive foreign use and exploitation: contract API/SLA schedules, foreign IP-address and user-access logs, hosting records, and periodic utilization reports confirming that the SaaS service was delivered and consumed entirely outside Colombia
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audit review focuses on the foreign domicile of the client, the effective destination of the service, and the timely collection of export proceeds in foreign currency. If the zero-rating is disallowed, DIAN issues an official assessment demanding 19% IVA on the full export consideration, plus moratory interest (intereses moratorios) at the Banco de la República certified rate and the inaccuracy penalty under Article 648 E.T., which is 100% of the omitted tax and rises to 200% where false, inexistent, or inexact invoices or documents are used. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days triggers separate foreign-exchange fines imposed under Banco de la República regulations. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating claims may be prosecuted as tax evasion under Article 402 of the Código Penal, carrying imprisonment of up to nine years plus fines, and can lead to suspension or cancellation of the RUT and exporter status, together with disqualification from future VAT refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) and the Foreign Exchange Department of the National Tax and Customs Directorate (DIAN) / Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism — but mainly Banco de la República operates FX control under Law 9 of 1991 and External Circular DCIN-83 of 2023 (as amended). The Colombian FX regime is administered by Banco de la República as the central bank, with day-to-day control by the Foreign Exchange Sub-Directorate of DIAN for enforcement. Also, the Colombian Association of Financial Institutions (Asobancaria) not regulatory. So full name: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), with regulatory enforcement by DIAN's Foreign Exchange Sub-Directorate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with full current account convertibility (goods, services, royalties, software licenses) but residual exchange control through the 'canalización' (channeling) of foreign exchange through authorized intermediaries (mercado cambiario). Capital account operations require registration with Banco de la República (Form No. 5 for foreign investment). Profit remittances/dividends are freely remittable subject to prior registration of foreign investment and withholding tax (7% dividends rate for resident beneficiaries; 33% for non-resident on post-tax distribution net of withholding, actually 10% 2025... hmm; need to be careful). The key: no surrender requirement but channeling mandatory for export proceeds above 10,000 USD. There are no hard capital controls, but there's a mandatory channeling rule: FX operations over US$10,000 (or equivalent) must be channeled through the FX market (mercado cambiario).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be channeled through the foreign exchange market (mercado cambiario) within a maximum term of 6 months following the date of collection... actually, under Decree 1999 of 2019, the deadline for channeling export proceeds was extended to 6 months from the date of shipment/export. For software services exports (ISIC 6201 — SaaS), the rule: services exports (exportación de servicios) must be channeled within 3 months? Let me recall: Under Decree 1369/2020? Actually Colombia's rule: exporters of goods have 6 months to channel proceeds. For services, there is no fixed surrender deadline previously; but Circular DCIN-83 established that proceeds from export of services must be channeled within a period... Under the current regime (Decree 1999 of 2019, amended by Decree 1369 of 2020), the term for channeling export proceeds of goods is 6 months from the date of shipment (embarque). For services, the term is counted from the date of receipt? Actually, for services exports, the channeling term is 6 months from the date the service is paid/collection? I need to state accurately: The statutory window is six (6) months from the date of shipment (goods) or from the date of accrual/notification of the operation (services), as per the external exchange regulations. There is no compulsory conversion/mandatory surrender ratio into pesos — proceeds may be kept in foreign currency in domestic bank accounts (cuentas de compensación) or abroad, but must be channeled through the official FX market. Actually, there is no mandatory conversion: You can keep USD. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% — there is no forced surrender; however, channeling is mandatory to finalize the operation. Also, through the 'cuenta de compensación' (compensation account) regime, overseas income can be held and used abroad; the surplus over USD 10,000 must be channeled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine from 1 to 5 SMMLV (approx. USD 300–1,500) plus surcharge for late payment; persistent non-renewal triggers administrative strike-off and cancellation of commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Deposition (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholders' meeting approval (approval must occur by March 31); effective deadline April 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to 10 SMMLV (approx. USD 3,000) and ineligibility to bid for public contracts; long-term non-deposition may lead to regulatory oversight action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Report (Reporte de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after filing the corporate income tax return (typically by mid-May; exact date depends on NIT last digit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to 15,000 UVT (approx. USD 190,000) under Article 651 of the Tax Code or penalty equivalent to 1% of net assets; failure may also trigger UBO status investigations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Recording of Minutes (Actas de la Asamblea/Reunión de Socios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records – Registered Agent / Corporate Records (not filed with government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held no later than March 31 each fiscal year; minutes must be registered in the minute book immediately after meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold and record the meeting invalidates financial statement approval, exposes directors to civil liability, and may constitute grounds for judicial dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (revisor fiscal) required if (i) total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.7 million) or gross revenue exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1 million); (ii) the company is subject to surveillance by Superintendencia de Sociedades; or (iii) it publicly offers securities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Reporting Standards (NIIF/IFRS) as adopted under Law 1314/2009; small and medium entities apply the simplified 'NIIF para PYMES' (Group 3) unless size thresholds require full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must annually file with DIAN a comprehensive report identifying every natural person with 5% or more ownership or control, including any share transfer effects recorded in the Register of Members up to December 31. The filing is made within one month after the annual income tax return and must reflect all UBO changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registro de Administradores/Revisor Fiscal)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas/Registro de Asamblea)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a standard S.A.S. engaged in B2B enterprise SaaS. Effective rate may be lowered through (i) the 100% additional income tax deduction for qualifying research, development and technology-innovation investments (CTeI), (ii) the preferential 20% CIT rate for taxpayers operating under an approved Free Trade Zone (Zona Franca) project involving software development and export services, and (iii) VAT exclusion applicable to pure software licensing income, which does not itself reduce CIT. Exempt income regimes for software exports may apply only if the company proves economic substance and statutory compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: DIAN Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios for legal entities); filed electronically through the MUISCA portal using DIAN-issued digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return; interim quarterly/prepaid CIT installments are payable over the taxable year as determined by DIAN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, the annual CIT return is due between 1 October and 31 October of the following tax year, with the exact deadline assigned according to the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. Non-calendar fiscal years follow the equivalent month after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIT, legal entity type, filing reason code, fiscal year start and end dates, and primary CIIU economic activity code (6201 for software development, 6202 for SaaS activities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers are assigned a DIAN NIT and must identify themselves as 'no residente sin establecimiento permanente' where applicable; the box must clearly state the Colombian agent or PE if one exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total gross income from B2B SaaS subscriptions, license fees, maintenance, implementation services, and consulting derived from Colombian and foreign customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Colombian-source income for non-residents without a PE; cross-border SaaS fees earned wholly abroad are generally outside the Colombian CIT return unless rendered through a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs: payroll, cloud infrastructure, hosting, third-party subcontractors, software amortization, Stripe/Wise payment processing fees, rent, and professional services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a PE should allocate direct and indirect expenses attributable to the Colombian PE and keep contemporaneous documentation for apportionment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only statutory exempt income, e.g. qualifying software export revenues or CTeI-derived income, after verifying the specific legal requirements and supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers generally cannot claim Colombian exempt-income benefits unless a DTA or special law grants them; include a detailed annex when claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida gravable after ordinary deductions, special deductions, and prior-year loss compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, this box must reflect only Colombian-source taxable income reduced by properly allocated expenses; treaty limitations should be referenced in the return annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply non-refundable credits including foreign tax credits, VAT on certain capital assets as a tax credit, and di minimis industry credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may apply treaty withholding tax credits or provisions only if a certificate of tax residence and beneficial ownership evidence are attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 78 / Final CIT assessed / balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate final income tax at 35% (or applicable preferential rate), subtract prepayments and withholdings, and report the resulting balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents subject to final withholding on a gross basis, this box should show zero additional tax if the withholding has fully satisfied the tax obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers the Article 641 ET penalty of 5% of the tax assessed per month or fraction of a month, capped at 100% of the tax; where no tax is due, fixed penalties measured in UVT apply. Errors or omissions generating understatement are penalized at up to 100% of the understated tax, plus daily moratory interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax on distributions made to non-resident shareholders when the distributed profits have already been subjected to the 35% corporate income tax. Distributions made out of profits not previously taxed may be re-characterized and subjected to an additional 35% corporate level tax plus the 10% recipient-level withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty-reduced dividend/interest/royalty rates, the non-resident payee must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate from the competent authority of the DTA jurisdiction, (ii) submit an original or apostilled certificate to the Colombian withholding agent before payment, (iii) complete and sign a beneficial-ownership and limitation-on-benefits declaration, and (iv) in cases where the statutory rate was applied, file an electronic refund claim before DIAN using the online solicitud de devolución/compensación within the applicable limitation period. DTA relief is denied when the foreign recipient is a conduit arrangement lacking economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-treaty withholding rates: interest paid to foreign financial institutions is generally 15%; interest paid to unrelated non-financial creditors is subject to the general 35% rate. Royalties and software license fees paid to non-residents are generally 35%, except certain technical services or technology-transfer payments that may qualify for the 15% withholding regime under Article 408 ET. Available DTAs may reduce interest to 0-10% and royalties to 5-15%, subject to substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory TP documentation (Local File, Master File, and TP Informative Return) is triggered when the taxpayer's gross income or total assets reach the annual indexed threshold, set at 135,000 UVT (COP 6,353,775,000 for tax year 2024), or when the value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds the statutory materiality threshold. Lower thresholds apply for transactions with related entities located in non-cooperative jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia applies anti-avoidance rules that require transactions to have genuine economic substance. While there is no separate ESR code of the Caribbean type, the DIAN may disregard transactions or re-characterize entities under the general anti-avoidance rule where the structure is artificial, lacks business purpose, or is used to avoid Colombian tax. A Colombian S.A.S. engaged in B2B SaaS must demonstrate adequate personnel, actual office or infrastructure, decision-making, control of core functions, and commercial substance for IP, license, and service transactions; mere invoicing or license-holding status is fatal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying B2B SaaS revenues, underreporting Stripe/Wise cross-border collections, inflating deductible costs, or intentionally omitting Colombian-source income in the Form 210.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN re-assessment at 35% plus moratory interest; accuracy penalty equal to 100% of the understated tax; criminal prosecution under Article 434 of Law 599/2000 with imprisonment of 36 to 108 months and fines up to 10,000 minimum legal monthly wages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under Article 59 of Law 1607/2012, holding directors and controlling shareholders jointly and severally liable. Directors who sign false returns face personal criminal indictment, preventive travel bans, asset embargoes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an S.A.S. purely as a pass-through license vehicle with no employees, physical location, operational activity, or commercial risk in Colombia, or interposing it to claim tax incentives or divert profits to a related low-tax entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN disregard of the legal entity, reallocation of income to the real beneficial owner, a surcharge on the reassessed tax, ineligibility for refunds, and administrative cancellation of the RUT tax registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and legal representatives become personally liable for the full corporate tax debt when the entity is treated as a sham. Criminal investigations may result in travel bans, asset freezing, and disqualification from acting as a director in Colombia.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Beneficial Ownership Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving high-volume SaaS subscription payments without verifying business counterparties, failing to report final beneficial owners to the UIAF, converting crypto or cash payments through Stripe/Wise without source explainability, or structuring transactions to avoid AML thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under Articles 323/324 of the Colombian Penal Code with imprisonment of 10 to 30 years and fines up to 50,000 minimum monthly legal wages; UIAF and DIAN administrative sanctions for non-reporting of beneficial ownership or AML deficiencies up to COP 1.8 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be prosecuted as co-authors or negligent parties for failing to implement AML controls. Preventive measures include travel bans and Interpol notices, high personal fines, and corporate dissolution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling software subscriptions or licensing rights to a foreign related party at prices below arm's length, inflating intercompany cloud-host fees, or failing to file the annual Transfer Pricing Informative Return and contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN adjustment to the arm's length price, additional 35% tax, moratory interest, and transfer pricing sanctions under Articles 260-8 and 260-19 ET, including penalties up to 2% of the value of related-party transactions (minimum 1,000 UVT), or up to 20,000 UVT for non-submission of required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who sign false transfer pricing documentation may be held personally civilly liable for the resulting tax damage; criminal liability arises when false documents are used to evade tax, triggering travel bans, extradition risk, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident beneficial owner without the mandatory withholding, incorrectly applying a treaty rate without a valid TRC, or distributing untaxed profits without the additional corporate-level charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN collection of the unwithheld tax, a penalty of 100% of the omitted withholding, and moratory interest; the local payer remains jointly liable for the full amount due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or cause a prohibited distribution without withholding are jointly liable to the tax authority; criminal tax fraud charges can be brought where the non-withholding is an intentional mechanism to strip profits from Colombia, with applicable custodial sentences and travel restrictions.
